missionPremise.ruling: OPS-16 amendment A-020, ruled 2026-08-19. Scoring was never a standing capability in this portfolio: twelve county writers exist in hauska-engine and three scorer CLIs in legacy-design-tools, and every other ledger row that exists was produced by a one-off lane script run once. There was no recompute route until this week because there was nothing to re-run.

freeFindingsAtCp1.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
freeFindingsAtCp1.finding: countyCoverageScoreCli.ts writes facet 'land-use'. No rail_key 'land-use' exists; the rail is 'landuse'. readManifestGrid joins county_facet_coverage on c.facet = r.rail_key, so those 19 rows join to NOTHING and have never rendered a cell.
freeFindingsAtCp1.evidence: live: facet 'land-use' has 19 rows, last_checked 2026-08-05, rail_state NULL on all 19; facet 'landuse' has 254 rows written by score_cad_rails_fast.mjs. county_rail has rail_key 'landuse', no 'land-use'.
freeFindingsAtCp1.implication: the only checked-in land-use scorer has been a silent no-op on the grid since the rail dimension was written. A scorer whose facet key does not match a rail key must be a hard failure, not a silent orphan.
freeFindingsAtCp1.ownedBy: SS-W13 (correctness in existing CLIs) -- SS-W12 mechanizes the GUARD, does not edit that file

freeFindingsAtCp1.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
freeFindingsAtCp1.finding: live county_rail says atom_family_state='present' AND has_writer=true for all 14 rails, including rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines and rail-corridor. The checked-in COUNTY_RAIL_DECLARATION (lib/db/src/schema/countyRailDimension.ts) declares those three atomFamilyState 'missing' with writerRef null.
freeFindingsAtCp1.implication: the DB dimension has drifted stale-OPTIMISTIC against the checked-in declaration -- the exact drift class that file's own header says it exists to prevent. Consequence: those cells render 'not-yet' (a promise) rather than 'no-atom' (an honest absence).
freeFindingsAtCp1.ownedBy: reported, not fixed here -- a declaration refresh is a ruling, not a lane side effect (DEV_PROCESS 5.4)

freeFindingsAtCp1.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
freeFindingsAtCp1.finding: score_cad_rails_fast.mjs clamps with Math.min(100, (n/feat)*100) and classifies every below-threshold cell 'needs-crosswalk'. countyGeometryScoreCli.ts's own header names the clamp as defect SF-25 and fails overcount closed to not-yet with the honest unclamped ratio.
freeFindingsAtCp1.implication: two live instruments disagree on the same rule. 762 owner/landuse/cad rows carry clamped values and a classification that means 'the join key is too thin to prove', which is not what a below-threshold atom count means.
freeFindingsAtCp1.ownedBy: SS-W12 mechanizes the correct behaviour in the shared engine so a rail declaration cannot reintroduce the clamp; re-scoring those rows is SS-W13/SS-W14 territory

freeFindingsAtCp1.label: VERIFIED by SS-W12
freeFindingsAtCp1.finding: naming footgun: in the scorer CLIs, env DATABASE_URL means the ATOMS store (hauska-prod-497015/hauska_mcp); in api-server, DATABASE_URL means the DEPLOYMENT store (legacy-design-tools-prod/neondb).
freeFindingsAtCp1.implication: one env name, two opposite meanings, in one repo. New code in this lane uses ATOMS_DATABASE_URL explicitly and never relies on the overloaded name.

design.oneLine: A rail becomes scoreable by DECLARING how it is measured, in checked-in data, against a small set of named measurement kinds; one shared engine turns a declaration plus a measurement into a ledger row; one generic CLI and one HTTP route trigger it.

parts.name: railScoringRegistry.ts
parts.role: DATA. One entry per rail key, covering ALL 14 rails -- including the six with no measurement spec, declared kind 'unspecified' with a reason and a spec owner (SS-W14). Unmentioned is the failure state; out-of-scope is a required classification (DEV_PROCESS 3.3).
carries: denominator spec: kind + prose counting rule (REQUIRED)
doesNotCarry: thresholdPct -- derived from COUNTY_RAIL_DECLARATION by railKey so thresholds have exactly one home (DEV_PROCESS 2.4)

parts.name: railScoreEngine.ts
parts.role: PURE core plus one shared upsert. Turns (rule, threshold, measurement, optional absence determination) into a ledger row. Enforces, in ONE place, the rules every per-rail scorer would otherwise re-implement: no clamping (overcount fails closed to not-yet with the honest unclamped ratio, SF-25); satisfied-absent only on a positive determination carrying a basis (L7 / DEV_PROCESS 4.3); facet always equals railKey; threshold always from the rail declaration.
parts.classifier: imports classifyFacet from countyCoverageScoreCli.ts (the existing single definition, already imported by the geometry and flood CLIs) rather than duplicating it (DEV_PROCESS 6.2). SS-W13 owns that file, so this lane pins the behaviours it depends on in its OWN test file -- if SS-W13 changes the classifier, SS-W12's tests fail loudly instead of SS-W12's behaviour drifting silently.

parts.name: railScoreProvenance.ts
parts.role: The denominator travels WITH the number (DEV_PROCESS 1.1/1.2). Canonical provenance string written into the existing artifact_path column, with a formatter, a parser and a round-trip test -- a contract, not a convention. NO schema change: see scopeBasis.

parts.name: countyRailScoreCli.ts
parts.role: One generic CLI replacing the per-rail CLI pattern. --rail=<key> (repeatable, or --all-scoreable), --county=<fips>, --dry-run. Reports per-rail numerator/denominator/basis and a VALUE delta.

parts.name: routes/countyRailScore.ts
parts.role: POST /api/county-ledger/score, service token, advisory lock, dryRun -- deliberately the SAME shape as SS-W7's POST /api/county-ledger/recompute, mounted under the SAME /county-ledger prefix as a second router so countyLedger.ts is not touched at all (PR #437 is open and owns that file).

design.idempotencyContract: Re-runnable is not 'the upsert has ON CONFLICT'. checked_at/last_verified_at move every run, so an upsert always looks like a change. The engine reads the existing row BEFORE writing and diffs by VALUE (excluding the two timestamps), reporting cellsChanged / cellsUnchanged. A second run against unchanged sources must report cellsChanged = 0. That is the machine-checkable claim, and it is tested. Same discipline as SS-W7's rule that a re-read must never masquerade as a recompute.
design.twoLegsNotOne: SS-W7's recompute is the SCORED to SERVED leg (county_facet_coverage -> county_ledger_snapshot). SS-W12's scorer is the WRITTEN to SCORED leg (atoms/parcel tables -> county_facet_coverage). They compose; they are not rivals. Coordination is: same auth, same lock discipline, same dryRun semantics, same before/after readback, same prefix -- a sibling route, not a second entry point.

adversarialReview.challenge: Is a registry actually data, or is it code wearing a data costume?
adversarialReview.answer: Honest split, stated plainly: adding a rail whose measurement kind ALREADY EXISTS is a declaration edit and nothing else. Adding a rail that needs a NEW kind is a new function against a narrow interface plus a declaration edit. Claiming otherwise would be the failure mode DEV_PROCESS 0 names. The registry says which of the two a given rail is.

adversarialReview.challenge: The route cannot score atom-count rails in production today -- api-server has no connection to the ATOMS store (verified: no ATOMS_DATABASE_URL, no atoms pool anywhere in artifacts/api-server/src). Shipping it risks a permanently-red control (DEV_PROCESS 2.0).
adversarialReview.answer: It fails CLOSED and NAMED: rails it cannot measure are reported as railsUnavailable with reason 'atoms_store_not_configured', never scored as zero and never silently skipped. The response tells the operator exactly what to wire. The moment ATOMS_DATABASE_URL exists on the service, every atom-count rail becomes scoreable with no code change. An invisible gap becomes a visible one.

adversarialReview.challenge: Proving the capability by writing to the live ledger would be the fastest proof.
adversarialReview.answer: Refused. Proof is a READ-ONLY dry run: the harness recomputes rails that already have ledger rows and is compared against what the one-off scripts stored. Pre-registered band: harness == stored for geometry and flood; harness >= stored for owner/landuse/cad wherever the one-off's Math.min clamp bit. A result outside the band is a finding either way (DEV_PROCESS 4.5).

adversarialReview.challenge: Why not port the three existing CLIs onto the harness and delete them?
adversarialReview.answer: SS-W13 is fixing correctness bugs in exactly those files this week. Rewriting them underneath that lane is a guaranteed collision and would make both closes unreadable. This lane is ADDITIVE: new files only, plus a two-line mount. The port is named as the follow-on, with its owner, in the close.

inScope: the scoring capability: registry, engine, provenance contract, generic CLI, HTTP route, tests, and a read-only equivalence proof against the live ledger

two other lanes have open PRs in this repo and drizzle migrations are sequentially numbered (SS-W7 already took 0082); a third concurrent migration is a merge-order hazard, and it would also require refreshing the schema fixture template and the hardcoded-list CI. The denominator requirement is met without one, via the checked-in declaration plus a parseable provenance contract in the existing artifact_path column.

completionPredicate: A stranger can add a new rail's coverage measurement by editing one declaration file (when its measurement kind exists) and running one command, and can re-run any rail's scoring at will and see, from the run's own report, what moved and what did not. Mechanized guards exist for: registry-vs-rail-dimension divergence, facet-key-equals-rail-key, no clamping, absence-requires-a-basis, and threshold-from-one-source. Nothing merged, nothing deployed, nothing written to the live ledger.
